verdict.rationale: Docs and runtime probes show a full pipeline for this story: raw content/conversations are ingested and auto-extracted into memories (docs-1, docs-10), memories are searchable via hybrid semantic search (docs-2, docs-28), and container tags let a developer scope memories per user/session so context persists and is retrievable later (docs-4, docs-24, docs-27, docs-25). A live runtime probe confirms the documented v3 search API is real and key-gated, not just paper docs (supermemory-probe-rt-2). One community complaint about oversized link content failing ingestion (supermemory-comm-1) is a real caveat but doesn't contradict the core add/retrieve-memory flow. Missing for 10: independent benchmarks or hands-on validation of retrieval quality/accuracy across long-running sessions beyond vendor-run MemoryBench.
